name: Channels
label: Dischord
lede: J. Robbins and Janet Morgan put two lead voices in a trio with Darren Zentek, made one album, and stopped in 2006 when their baby son was diagnosed with SMA. Ten years later they came back with a single named for a face that needs slapping.

eras.title: Robbins, his wife and a drummer from Kerosene 454
eras.text: By 2003 J. Robbins had already fronted Jawbox and Burning Airlines. Channels put his wife Janet Morgan on bass and a second lead voice, with Darren Zentek of Kerosene 454 behind the kit.

years.h: Janet Morgan takes co-lead vocals in J. Robbins' new trio
years.p: [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] plays guitar, [[Janet Morgan|1f7ee7d4-46bf-4f6b-829f-14c1e30a4e8f]] bass and [[Darren Zentek|68c31f7f-f2e8-4353-92b7-c7ebf47f404d]] drums. Morgan sings co-lead, not backup, which changes the shape of a Robbins song.
years.xp:
Zentek came from [[Kerosene 454|3689eda0-1b6d-43f3-83ad-e58211ae7a3a]] and [[Oswego|43bb29f2-9915-4465-99d0-72d3ff99bfa7]]. Robbins was by then one of the busiest producers in the region, and the band's recordings would pass through his own Magpie Cage studio in Baltimore.

Wikipedia calls Channels the home of Robbins' most overtly political writing. The song titles to come point the same way: "To the New Mandarins," "Unreal Estates," "New Logo."

yt: Fear Is a Man's Best Friend, the John Cale cover
years.h: The Open EP comes out on DeSoto, with a John Cale cover
years.p: The D.C. label DeSoto Records, which had released [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]] and later [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] records, puts out Channels' first record. Dischord carries it in distribution.

eras.title: One album, then a diagnosis
eras.text: The debut album came out on Dischord in 2006. Months later Robbins and Morgan's baby son was diagnosed with a serious genetic disease, and the band went on indefinite hiatus.

years.h: Waiting for the Next End of the World, Dischord No. 151
years.p: Twelve songs recorded at Magpie Cage, Phase and Inner Ear, produced by the band with Freeman Moxy. Titles include "Helen Mirren" and "$99.99."
play: Waiting for the Next End of the World

years.h: Callum Robbins is diagnosed with SMA and Channels goes quiet
years.p: Janet Morgan's words to NPR, after her and J. Robbins' son Callum, nine months old, was diagnosed with Type 1 spinal muscular atrophy in September 2006. Dischord says the band went on indefinite hiatus that year.
years.xp:
SMA is a genetic motor neuron disease. Morgan told NPR the news came as two blows at once, the diagnosis and the prognosis. Robbins told the network he expected Callum to grow into a bright, sociable kid who would not be mobile.

Dischord's page for the benefit compilation explains the money problem: the alternative therapies the family was pursuing weren't covered by insurance.

eras.title: The scene shows up for Callum
eras.text: Washington's music community answered with benefit shows, reunions and a compilation. Robbins kept producing and kept a band going with Zentek under a new name.

years.h: Callum turns one, and a benefit compilation takes shape
years.p: Dischord notes Callum Robbins turned 1 in January 2007. The Cultural Society, Catlick Records and Letterbox put together For Callum, with proceeds going straight to Robbins and Morgan.

years.h: The Dismemberment Plan gets back together for Callum
years.p: Punknews reported the [[Dismemberment Plan|1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c]] would reunite to help pay for Callum Robbins' care. A recording of their April 28, 2007 Black Cat show still circulates, and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]] reunited for a Callum benefit too.
years.xp:
The Washington Post's Express listed an Owls & Crows benefit for Callum in January 2007. NPR's July 2007 story, headlined as indie rockers rallying around one of their own, followed the family and the shows.

Bands that had split for years came back for a single night because a friend's kid needed care.

years.h: One opening slot for The Bomb becomes [[Office of Future Plans|f57177fc-474e-4488-8b04-3ef43cfce8ed]]
years.p: Dischord says The Bomb asked J. Robbins to open their Baltimore show in fall 2009. The one-time set grew into a band: Robbins, Darren Zentek, Brooks Harlan on bass and Gordon Withers on cello and guitar.

years.h: Dischord releases the Office of Future Plans album
years.p: [[Office of Future Plans|f57177fc-474e-4488-8b04-3ef43cfce8ed]]' self-titled record is Dischord No. 173. Robbins and Zentek also play with [[Vic Bondi|3761c6de-75f8-4c9b-931e-fd6a593594a0]] as Report Suspicious Activity.

eras.title: A second life, timed to an inauguration
eras.text: The EP came back on clear vinyl, and then the band did. Channels reunited in 2016 and put out its first new music in a decade the week Donald Trump took office.

years.cap: J. Robbins on guitar, Darren Zentek behind him, at the Rock N' Roll Hotel, Washington, D.C., May 30, 2014
years.h: Open returns on clear vinyl, ten years on
years.p: Channels' 2004 EP gets a limited clear-vinyl 10-inch with a CD, per Discogs.

years.cap: Janet Morgan singing and playing bass at the Rock N' Roll Hotel, Washington, D.C., May 30, 2014
years.h: "It clicked like they had never even taken a break"
years.p: Dischord's words for what happened when J. Robbins, Janet Morgan and Darren Zentek started writing again in 2016, Robbins and Morgan in Baltimore, Zentek in D.C. Above all, the label says, it was fun.

years.h: Three days after the inauguration comes "Backpfeifengesicht"
years.p: Channels' first new music in a decade, a 7-inch on Free Criminal Records with "Airstrip One" on the B-side. Bandcamp Daily translated the German title as a face in need of a slap and called it an anti-Trump protest single.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily's Jes Skolnik wrote that Channels' intimate knowledge of Washington made the politics feel natural rather than opportunistic, and marked the single as the start of the band's second life.

"Airstrip One" takes its title from the name Orwell gave Britain in Nineteen Eighty-Four.
